one_liner: Lark Open Platform offers a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0 user authorization and tenant tokens, self-serve app creation on any plan including free, and an official MCP server.
auth_notes: user_access_token via authorization-code OAuth flow with refresh tokens; tenant_access_token obtained by exchanging app_id/app_secret (app-level, client-credentials-like). Custom apps need admin approval of scopes within a tenant.
access_notes: Developer Console lets anyone in an org create a custom app; works on any Lark plan including free/Starter (10,000 basic API calls/month on Starter). Scopes require tenant admin approval, which a developer can self-do in their own free tenant.
blocker_notes: Minor: scopes need tenant admin approval, and Starter plan caps basic API calls at 10,000/month; neither blocks building.

evidence.quote: OAuth token API for acquiring the `user_access_token` and `refresh_token`. The `user_access_token` serves as the user's access credential, which allows API calls to be made on behalf of the user.
This API is used to initiate user authorization. After the user consents to the authorization, the application will receive an authorization code, referred to as `code`.
Any Lark plan, including Starter. Custom apps can call the Lark API on every plan.
The total number of basic API calls for all enterprise self-built applications under a single tenant is limited to **10,000 times per month**
The Free plan supports up to 20 users and natively bundles unlimited chats with 18 months history, structured wikis, 100 GB storage
When calling the server API, you need to include the access token in the request header `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`.
This is the Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool designed to help users quickly connect to the Feishu/Lark platform
Lark Open Platform provides a remote MCP Server configuration feature that supports the Streamable HTTP transmission protocol
